name: Ferrari 166 MM Barchetta
description:
The car that made Ferrari's name, and it is named after the race: MM for Mille Miglia, which a 166 had won in 1948 before this body existed.

Touring of Milan drew the shape and built it Superleggera — hand-beaten alloy over a frame of thin tubes — and when it was shown at Turin in 1948 a journalist said it looked less like a car than a little boat. Barchetta stuck, and the shape it named was copied for a decade, the Austin Healey and the AC Ace among the copies.

Underneath sat Gioacchino Colombo's two-litre V12, single overhead camshaft per bank, three Webers, about 140 hp in a car of some 650 kg. In 1949 Clemente Biondetti won the Mille Miglia with one and Luigi Chinetti won Le Mans with another, driving all but a few minutes of the twenty-four hours himself. Thirty-odd were built.
author: PedroBLR
